editorial.description_en: A deep pool in a river where the current stops. Dark, cool, and closer to blue than to green.
editorial.description_ja: 川の淵のような、深く青みのある緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.446, C 0.046, h 190.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 淵 (fuchi, a deep pool) + 水 (mizu, water). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Pool Water" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 淵水. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — tetsu-midori at ΔE00 7.7, iwa-goke at ΔE00 9.6, yama-kage at ΔE00 12.9. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (10°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
